outcome: Routine case enrichment and a defined set of low-risk actions run automatically, freeing analysts for the cases that need judgement.
overview: Government security teams are usually short of analysts rather than short of alerts, and the first hour of most investigations is the same handful of lookups performed by hand. FortiSOAR with FortiSIEM turns those into playbooks: enrichment runs automatically, the case arrives with context attached, and a defined set of low-risk actions can be taken without waiting for a human. What is deliberately not automated is anything that changes the estate without approval. The value is measured in analyst minutes returned per case, and it only appears where the triage process was written down first.

benefits.text: Repeated enrichment steps run automatically, so a case arrives with its context already gathered
benefits.limits: Automating an undocumented process encodes whatever the last analyst happened to do; the playbook is only as good as the triage process behind it

benefits.text: A defined set of low-risk responses can be executed without waiting for an analyst
benefits.limits: The action set must be explicitly bounded and approved; an automated action that changes the estate without approval is a governance failure, not a time saving

benefits.text: Case handling becomes consistent and auditable across shifts and analysts
benefits.limits: Consistency depends on every analyst actually working inside the recorded platform; a step taken through a side channel — a phone call, an ad hoc email — breaks the audit trail it is meant to produce

residency: Platform and case data run inside the entity’s own data centre, which is the standard requirement for government security operations in this region

notFor.situation: A team whose triage process is not documented
notFor.why: Automation encodes a process; where none is written down it encodes an accident and makes it repeatable

notFor.situation: A security operations function already running an orchestration platform
notFor.why: Playbooks do not port between platforms, so a second one means rebuilding the content

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner · Duration: 10–14 weeks to three case types automated in production
Support model: Vendor support for the platform; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional playbook retainer with an agreed monthly backlog.
1) Assessment — case-type inventory, handling-time baseline, process documentation state
2) Design — approved action set, playbook designs, connector requirements and the review path
3) Build — platform, connectors, first playbooks under version control
4) Operate and hand over — playbooks live on the agreed case types, analysts authoring unaided
deliverables: Every automated action falls inside the signed action set, verified by review of the playbook repository
A case record shows every step taken, whether by a playbook or a person
A playbook change goes through review before it reaches production
effort: 10–14 weeks to three case types automated in production
